result.markdown: --- title: "[Graph.single_source_all_shortest_paths()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method}" body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 toc-depth: 3 page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} List every shortest path from a source to each reachable node. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L42490-L42560){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python Graph.single_source_all_shortest_paths( source, weighted=None, ) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} ![Single-source all shortest paths](/assets/graphs/single-source-all-shortest-paths.light.svg){.lightbox fig-alt="A three-by-three grid A to I searched from the corner A (outlined). Badges count the shortest paths from A to each node; they add up like Pascal's triangle, so the far corner I has 6. The six 4-hop paths from A to I are drawn on the right as small copies of the grid, each path in the accent color." width="100%"} Where `single_source_shortest_path()` gives one shortest path per node, this method returns all of them, which matters whenever ties are common (unweighted graphs, grids, networks with integer costs): load balancing over equal-cost routes, counting alternatives, or checking how robust a route is. The number of shortest paths can grow exponentially with distance (a grid has binomially many), so use this on small graphs or short distances. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [source]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Union[int, str]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : The start node, as an ID or label. [weighted]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Whether to use edge weights. If `None` (default), follows the graph's `weighted` flag. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [dict[int, list[list[int]]]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : For every reachable node ID, its shortest paths as node ID lists, sorted (the source maps to `[[source]]`). ::: ## Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [ValueError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If the source does not exist or a negative cycle is reachable. ::: ## Technical Notes {.doc-technical-notes} The predecessor lists of `predecessor()` define a DAG whose source-to-node paths are exactly the shortest paths; they are enumerated by depth-first search. Matches NetworkX's `single_source_all_shortest_paths`. ## Examples {.doc-examples} In a 3 x 3 grid there are 6 shortest paths between opposite corners: ::: {#15eb5ce2 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec grid = ec.Graph().add_grid_2d(3, 3) ids = sorted(grid.get_node_ids(limit=None)) paths = grid.single_source_all_shortest_paths(ids[0]) len(paths[ids[-1]]) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` 6 ``` ::: :::
